tools.name: search_decisions
tools.description: Search the decision records by title, tags or body text, newest first. Returns each match with its status, tags, date and a snippet, so an open or superseded decision is visible without reading the file. Use read_adr for the full text of a hit. An empty result means nothing matched; check the 'available' field — false means there was no corpus to search, not that nothing matched.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the project's written knowledge — the architecture documents, the skills, the capability specifications and the decision records — and return matching files with a path and a snippet. Narrow the search with the scope argument: decisions, architecture, skills, specs or all. An empty result means nothing matched; check the 'available' field — false means the corpus was not searched at all.

tools.name: search_tasks
tools.description: Search tasks by title (case-insensitive).

tools.name: smart_rewrite
tools.description: Craft a concise, actionable task title from a raw idea.

tools.name: suggest_tags
tools.description: Suggest tags for a note.

tools.name: summarize_note
tools.description: Summarize a note in one sentence.

tools.name: update_adr
tools.description: Change an existing ADR's status frontmatter; the body is never modified. status must be one of: accepted, deferred, superseded, open. status=superseded additionally requires supersededBy, naming an existing slug (a markdown link is accepted). Use this to close a decision once it is settled, and to mark one as replaced after writing its successor — the replacement is a separate write_adr call, not a new '-v2' slug of this one.

tools.name: update_note
tools.description: Updates an existing note's title and/or body.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Updates an existing project.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Updates an existing task. Pass only fields to change.

tools.name: weekly_plan
tools.description: Suggest 3-5 tasks to focus on this week.

tools.name: write_adr
tools.description: Create a NEW Architecture Decision Record (ADR) as a Markdown file. Fails if the slug already exists — a decision is never overwritten. To close or revise an existing decision use update_adr, which changes its status and records the supersedes/superseded-by link. To say something new that replaces an old decision, write a new ADR naming the old one in its `supersedes:` frontmatter field, then call update_adr on the old one with status=superseded — do NOT invent a '-v2' slug, it leaves the predecessor unlinked.
